budget_items.topic: Sum of proposed stormwater fees across all properties
budget_items.what_was_said: The consolidated spreadsheet's fee column was summed across all properties to see what the ERU-based fee schedule would raise in total.
The per-ERU fee used in the spreadsheet was described as changeable depending on the final budget target for the program.
It was suggested the per-ERU fee could come down significantly in a future iteration if the budget requirement is reduced, making it more palatable to residents.
A task force member noted their own household's estimated annual fee under the current model.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member ran the town's property tax calculator assuming the stormwater program were funded through the operating budget with a given increase, to see the effect on the average single-family tax bill versus shifting cost to commercial/industrial.
Based on the calculator, a member said the average home's increase would be somewhat higher than an earlier estimate.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Crossing tax bill and assessment
budget_items.what_was_said: Members looked up the shopping center's current tax bill and assessed value, noting the assessment had fallen from the prior figure, to gauge how a stormwater utility fee would compare to its existing tax burden.

budget_items.topic: Per-acre tax comparison, Lunenburg Crossing vs. typical home
budget_items.what_was_said: Members compared per-acre tax payments between a large commercial property and a typical one-acre single-family home to argue commercial parcels pay less per acre.
A member gave their own per-acre tax figure to illustrate the gap between residential and commercial per-acre taxation.
Members discussed that administrative overhead for billing (integrating into MUNIS, similar to the sewer billing process) had originally been high and was negotiated down.

decisions.decision: For 400 Lemon(ster) Shirley Road (Mary Coburn/Edal property), the use code will be corrected/forced to code 4101 rather than left blank.
Woodlands condominiums and Stone Farm Estates will keep individual per-unit assessment rather than being billed as one global fee, since prior treatment made sense.
1295 Massachusetts Ave storage facility bays: the fee will be assigned to the overall property owner/manager rather than split among individual bay renters.
Tri-Town Apartments (use code 9960) will be billed as one combined fee to the owning entity rather than split by individual building/unit.
The Emerald Place property's impervious area will be combined with the adjacent Arrive property and billed as a single combined fee to the ownership entity.
Future task force meetings will be held on Microsoft Teams instead of Zoom, since the group already has Teams licensing and had recording trouble on Zoom.

Before asking Weston & Sampson for additional survey data, the task force will first check the town's older CI (commercial/industrial) spreadsheet to see if it already has the missing impervious-area figures.
A member will compile the list of properties needing reassessment/additional impervious-area data and send the questions to Weston & Sampson (via the consultant referred to as "J"/"Jice").

The task force leaned toward pursuing a stand-alone stormwater utility rather than funding the program through the operating budget, given the larger tax-bill impact and lost commercial cost-shifting under the operating-budget option.
Combining the sewer commission and a stormwater commission would require action by the state legislature, so this is not being pursued as a near-term option.
The list of properties lacking impervious-area data will simply be sent on to the consultant rather than reviewed line-by-line by the full task force first.
Next two task force meetings set for Monday, July 13th and Thursday, July 30th.

minutes.headline: Task force keeps refining property-by-property stormwater fee data and leans toward a utility, not the operating budget
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force spent nearly the entire meeting working line-by-line through a combined assessor/Weston & Sampson spreadsheet, assigning ERUs and fixing missing use codes, missing impervious-area data, and how condo/rental/HOA complexes should be billed. It also compared funding the program through the operating budget versus a stand-alone utility fee, leaning toward the utility option, and set next steps (checking an old CI spreadsheet, sending gaps to the consultant, finishing a bylaw draft) before a possible fall Town Meeting article.

what_happened.line: The task force leaned toward funding stormwater work through a stand-alone utility fee rather than the operating budget.
Members spent most of the meeting correcting property-by-property use codes and impervious-area data feeding the fee model.
The task force set billing rules combining fees for storage bays, apartments and adjoining lots, while keeping some condos billed per unit.
Combining the sewer and a new stormwater commission would need state legislative action, so it is not being pursued now.
Next task force meetings are set for July 13 and July 30, with a bylaw draft due before a possible fall Town Meeting article.

why_it_matters: Whether stormwater costs land on the tax bill or a separate utility fee changes how much residential versus commercial property owners pay.
The property-by-property review, including exceptions for condos, storage units and mixed-ownership sites, will determine each parcel's individual fee.
A fall Town Meeting article would ask voters to act on the funding mechanism and any bylaw the task force drafts.
